context:
Treat trust, moderation, and observability as first-class platform features.
The hosted explorer can be static-first, but the write path still needs the
same operational rigor as any public ingestion service.
description:
A hosted benchmark-results platform is not credible if anyone can spam it,
exfiltrate private metadata, or silently corrupt public read models. Before
BenchBox opens self-service submissions broadly, it needs threat modeling,
quotas, moderation controls, observability, backups, and explicit incident
procedures.

This item covers the operational and governance controls that make the hosted
platform safe to run in public.

**Phase assignment:** Phase 3 only. Phase 1 (static, maintainer-curated) and
Phase 2 (PR-based, GitHub-mediated) have no hosted services to secure or
operate. This work is only relevant if/when a hosted API is built.

anti_patterns.dont: launch self-service public submissions without quotas and rate limits
anti_patterns.instead: define throttling and eligibility rules first

anti_patterns.dont: rely on UI badges alone for trust and visibility enforcement
anti_patterns.instead: enforce policy at the service boundary
anti_patterns.why: storage and API mistakes can leak data

preserves.behavior: Explorer rebuilds and moderation actions remain auditable after the fact
Public and unlisted result visibility rules stay enforceable at the storage and API layers, not only in UI hints

verifications.description: Threat model document committed with STRIDE coverage (run after w2)
Incident runbook committed and covers all three required incident classes (run after w8)

work_units.notes:
List what must be protected: raw bundles, durable metadata, public read
models, API keys, actor identity records. Map external interfaces (submission
API, explorer, admin CLI). Output: one-page asset inventory used as input
to w2.
work_units.summary: Enumerate assets and attack surface: protected assets, external interfaces, trust boundaries

work_units.notes:
Apply STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure,
Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege) to each layer in w1. Output:
threat-model.md with per-threat likelihood × impact scores and proposed
mitigations.
work_units.summary: Write STRIDE threat analysis for the submission, storage, and explorer layers

work_units.notes:
Sort threats by risk score. For each top-10 mitigation, either assign to
an existing design TODO (auth, quota, moderation) or add it as an
acceptance criterion to the Phase 3 launch gate.
work_units.summary: Prioritize top 10 mitigations and assign to design items or Phase 3 acceptance criteria

work_units.notes:
Choose between API keys vs OAuth. Define token scopes (submit-only vs full
read access). Set session and refresh lifetime policy. Outputs feed into
integrate-benchbox-cli-submit-and-service-auth.
work_units.summary: Define auth model: eligibility gates, token type, scopes, and session lifetime

work_units.notes:
Set per-actor burst budget, daily submission cap, and total storage quota.
Define what happens when a limit is hit (reject vs queue vs alert). Include
a grace period for first-time submitters.
work_units.summary: Define rate limiting and quota model: per-actor submission limits and storage caps

work_units.notes:
How does a new actor become trusted? Who can trigger takedowns and under
what conditions? What fields does the audit log capture? Output: moderation
runbook with explicit escalation paths.
work_units.summary: Define moderation workflow: trust promotion, content takedown, and audit log schema

work_units.notes:
Set observable, testable SLO targets. Example targets: submission ACK <5s
p99, explorer p99 <500ms, backup RPO <24h, RTO <4h. These feed alerting
thresholds and incident severity definitions.
work_units.summary: Define platform SLOs: ingestion latency p99, explorer availability, backup RPO/RTO

work_units.notes:
Define who is alerted, what actions are taken, and what public
communications are required for each incident class. Runbook must be
executable without the original author present.
work_units.summary: Write incident response runbook for result integrity incidents, data breaches, and abuse
